Update from Newbury Innovation (Conor La Grue) — 24 Sep 2026
Subject: RE: Lift PCB Enquiry - Design and manufacture - SQR-45454

Conor La Grue of Newbury Innovation (Newbury Electronics' Innovation division) has taken over Sesame's lift PCB enquiry (SQR-45454). They have reviewed the feasibility study and control drawings and consider the concept feasible in principle, but need answers to seven clarification points on architecture, safety functions, MICO protection, LOGO! scope, build level and target time savings before giving an indicative NRE range. Once clarified they will provide a development cost range, after which a call would be the next step.

Action for Giles:
- Answer Newbury Innovation's clarification questions: confirm Option A as baseline with safety functions/conductors outside the PCB; whether the safety-switched 24 V rail stays outside the PCB; whether Murrelektronik MICO protection is incorporated on-PCB or kept discrete; whether the first-generation objective is wiring/termination consolidation around the Siemens LOGO! rather than addressing LOGO! I/O capacity; whether the first iteration is a populated/tested PCB assembly or a complete DIN/carrier-mounted module with production test fixture; whether the board stays an interface/distribution assembly or includes communications/remote diagnostics; and provide an estimate of current panel build/test hours or target assembly/service time to remove.
- Once answers are sent, expect an indicative NRE range from Newbury Innovation; if acceptable, arrange a call.
Issue: Newbury Innovation cannot provide an indicative NRE development cost range until Sesame answers seven clarification points on the PCB design scope and architecture.
